# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I need to communicate "green, orange, blue" order to Blind, but I can't speak (Blind can't see gestures anyway, and can't hear speech), and I can't touch the bomb. My only channel is gesture to Deaf, who can see but not hear. So Deaf must relay to Blind... but Deaf can't touch the bomb either, and Blind can't see gestures.

Wait - Deaf can see the bomb (colors/markings) but I hold the manual. I need to get "green, orange, blue" to Deaf via gesture, so Deaf can then match those colors on the bomb visually, and then Deaf needs to somehow inform Blind (who can't see gestures, can't hear). But Deaf also cannot speak? Let me check - only Mute is explicitly restricted from speaking. Deaf's restrictions: cannot hear, cannot touch. Deaf CAN speak presumably.

So chain: I gesture wire order to Deaf. Deaf sees bomb colors and gestures, matches order, then speaks the order to Blind (Blind can hear). That works.

I'll assign gesture symbols to colors: green=👍, orange=✌, blue=👌. I need to establish this code, but Deaf has no prior context. I'll send gestures in sequence with clear structure, trusting Deaf can infer sequence-then-match against manual convention once established. Since this is turn 1, I should just send the order using distinct gestures and hope to clarify meaning next round, or use a self-evident approach - perhaps gesture count-based coding isn't intuitive without prior agreement.

Given constraints, best effort: send three distinct gestures representing green, orange, blue in order, and plan to clarify via later rounds since Deaf will respond and we can build shared code over turns.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "✌", "👌"])
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I feel a strip with three symbols: two identical, one different. Keypad has 4 keys labeled 1,5,2,6, accepts 1 digit, nothing entered yet. There are 6 wires but I cannot tell them apart by touch. Need your manual info and Deaf's visual info to know which wire or key to act on.
Deaf says: I see: DISPLAY shows 9. LIGHT is blue. STRIP has three sections painted red, green, green in that order. KEYPAD is engraved with digit 1 shows 1, digit 2 shows 5, digit 3 shows 2, digit 4 shows 6, it accepts 1 digit entry, currently nothing entered. WIRES are numbered 1 through 6: white, purple, blue, red, orange, green. Mute, please tell me what the manual says we need to do.

Now I have real info. The manual says: cut green wire, then orange wire, then blue wire. Deaf sees wires numbered 1-6 with colors: 1 white, 2 purple, 3 blue, 4 red, 5 orange, 6 green. So order should be: wire 6 (green), then wire 5 (orange), then wire 3 (blue).

I need to convey this to Deaf via gesture since Deaf can see me but not hear me. Deaf can then relay to Blind by speech (Blind can hear). I need a gesture code for "green, then orange, then blue" or directly for wire numbers 6, 5, 3.

Since gestures only carry symbols, not numbers directly, I'll use finger-count-style gestures to represent numbers. I can use ☝ (1), ✌ (2), 🤟 (looks like 3 fingers), 🖐 (5), etc. Let me map digits to gesture symbols in a simple counting scheme: ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, ✋=4(or 🖐=5). Actually simplest: use ☝ repeated to indicate count, separated by 👋 as a separator gesture.

I'll gesture the sequence of wire numbers using repeated ☝ strokes separated by pause gesture 👋 as delimiter: 6 = six ☝, delimiter, 5 = five ☝, delimiter, 3 = three ☝.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports: display shows 9, light is blue, strip pattern red-green-green, wires in order are white,purple,blue,red,orange,green. Keypad keys are 1,5,2,6 needing 1 digit. What does the manual say to do given this?
Deaf says: Display dropped from 9 to 8, this looks like a countdown timer. Mute, I received three groups of tally-like gestures: six, five, three, separated by waves. Please confirm if these are numbers 6, 5, 3 or something else, and tell me what to do with the keypad or wires. Blind, stand by, do not touch anything yet.

Deaf correctly decoded 6, 5, 3 — that matches wire positions for green(6), orange(5), blue(3). The countdown is dropping (9→8), so time pressure is real; I need to confirm quickly and also address the keypad, but the manual I have only mentions wires, nothing about keypad or strip or display. I should confirm the numbers and clarify these are wire-cut order, and state I have no info on keypad/strip/display since manual only covers wires.

I need to confirm "yes, 6,5,3" via gesture. I'll use a simple thumbs-up ✌+👍 style: a clear affirmation gesture, then repeat the numbers to lock in, and signal "wire" concept isn't available in gesture-only, but Deaf already inferred these numbers correspond to wires since Blind mentioned wires numbered by Deaf's own list. Deaf should now speak the order to Blind: cut wire 6, then 5, then 3.

I'll gesture confirmation: 👍 (yes/correct), then repeat 6,5,3 once more for clarity, then a distinct gesture for "wires" — but no direct symbol for "wire". I'll trust context since Deaf already listed wires 1-6 and asked "what to do with keypad or wires" — I need to specify it's wires, not keypad. I'll use 🫱 (a reaching/pulling gesture, suggestive of wire-pulling) to hint "wire action", though this is guesswork. Better to keep it simple: confirm numbers correct, and use a repeated distinct gesture to mean "in this order, cut" — but no gesture for "cut" concretely. I'll rely on Deaf's own reasoning: since keypad only takes 1 digit and my numbers are three, they must be wire order, not keypad. Deaf should infer that. I'll just confirm.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Countdown is dropping, we are on a clock. I cannot see gestures, so please speak the instructions to me directly in words: tell me exactly what to press on keypad or what wire to cut, using the colors/numbers Deaf gave you: wires white,purple,blue,red,orange,green in order 1-6, keys 1,5,2,6, strip pattern red-green-green, light blue.
Deaf says: Urgent: DISPLAY hit 0 and LIGHT changed from blue to yellow, something just triggered. Mute confirmed the sequence is six five three. Blind, do not act yet. Mute, please confirm: is six five three a wire cutting order, or a code for the keypad, or something else? I need to know exactly what action to take before anyone touches anything.

Blind is asking me to speak directly - but I cannot speak at all, only gesture. I must rely on Deaf to relay to Blind via speech since Deaf can speak and Blind can hear.

Deaf is asking me to confirm what "six five three" means. I need to clarify: it's the wire cutting order (by wire position number), corresponding to green(6th wire), orange(5th wire), blue(3rd wire) — matching the manual's "cut green, then orange, then blue."

I need a gesture to distinguish "wire" vs "keypad". Let me use a clear distinct approach: point-based gesture. I'll use 🫲 (a grabbing/pulling hand, suggesting wire) repeated 3 times to mean "wire action", followed by the numbers again in the same order, to reinforce this is wire sequence not keypad digit entry (keypad only takes 1 digit, but I gave 3 numbers - that alone should disambiguate, but let me make it explicit).

I'll gesture: a "wire" indicator (using 🫲 three times to represent 3 wire actions) then the numbers 6,5,3 once more clearly separated.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫲","🫲","🫲","👋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝","☝","☝","👋","☝","☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Display hit 0, light changed blue to yellow. We need your answer now: is six-five-three a wire-cutting sequence (by wire number 1-6), a keypad code, or something else? Keypad only accepts 1 digit though, so a 3-digit sequence like 653 doesn't fit the keypad directly unless it's wire numbers. Please clarify urgently.
Deaf says: Mute's gesture now shows a cutting motion three times followed by six five three. I believe this means cut wires in order: wire six, then wire five, then wire three. Blind, wire six is green, wire five is orange, wire three is blue, but go by the numbers not colors since you cannot see color. Mute, if this is wrong, signal me immediately. Blind, wait for Mute's explicit confirmation before cutting, we have display now climbing from zero, count is at three.

Deaf has correctly interpreted my gesture: cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3. This exactly matches the manual (green=6, orange=5, blue=3). I need to confirm this is correct urgently since the situation is escalating (display climbing from zero).

I'll send a clear, simple, unambiguous confirmation gesture - a strong affirmative signal.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍","👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the green wire, then the orange wire,
then the blue wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf believes your gesture meant: cut wire 6, then wire 5, then wire 3, in that order. Display is climbing again, now at three. Please confirm explicitly if this is correct before I cut anything - I will not act until you confirm.
Deaf says: Confirmed twice by Mute with thumbs up. Blind, act now: cut wire six first, then wire five, then wire three, in that exact order. Light just turned red and display is climbing, this is urgent.

Deaf has confirmed and instructed Blind to act. My part is done — I've confirmed the correct sequence twice. There's nothing more for me to add unless something goes wrong. I'll wait and stay alert in case Blind or Deaf need further clarification.

```
wait()
```
